title: Prompt-MII: Meta-Learning Instruction Induction for LLMs
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Our method matches the accuracy of long-context in-context learning while using an order of magnitude fewer prompt tokens.
layout: 1 scatter plot, accuracy vs token cost, dashed line with compression callout
description: A single scatter and line plot titled 'Performance vs Prompt Length'. The x-axis is prompt length in tokens (0 to 12k) and the y-axis is F1 score (about 0.25 to 0.45). A blue line with triangle markers shows in-context learning for n=5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 examples. F1 rises from about 0.35 to 0.435 as the prompt grows from about 2k to 11k tokens. Three single points sit at low token counts. A red circle (Naive Instruction) is at the bottom left. An orange square (PromptMII-Zero) is at mid-height. A green diamond (PromptMII) is at the top left, at about 0.438. A grey dashed horizontal line links the green diamond to the n=100 triangle. A boxed label above it reads '13× compression'. A legend sits at the bottom right. The eye goes first to the green diamond and the dashed line.
caption: Classification task performance averaged over 90 datasets, using the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model. PROMPT-MII achieves performance comparable to ICL while using 13× fewer tokens.
abstract: A popular method to adapt large language models (LLMs) to new tasks is in-context learning (ICL), which is effective but incurs high inference costs as context length grows. In this paper we propose a method to perform instruction induction, where we take training examples and reduce them to a compact but descriptive prompt that can achieve performance comparable to ICL over the full training set. Specifically, we propose PROMPT-MII, a reinforcement learning (RL) based framework to meta-learn an instruction induction model that can generate compact instructions on the fly for an arbitrary new dataset. We train on over 3,000 diverse classification datasets from the HuggingFace hub, and evaluate on 90 unseen tasks. PROMPT-MII improves downstream model quality by 4-9 F1 points (10-20% relative), matching ICL performance while requiring 3-13x fewer tokens.
